work_order.understanding:
All three review findings from PR #67 were re-checked against current main (6ee19f7) and all three still reproduce. This version answers the two objections raised against the rejected v1 plan, both accepted in full.

Objection 1 (files[0].change contradicted AC-1): v1 said "rewrapped so every line is at most 79 characters, matching the width the surrounding comment block already uses", which permits a rewrap that splits the phrase AC-1 greps for. The reviewer measured that a greedy 71-column fill — the width lines 26-28 of this very block use — splits it. Fixed by removing the rewrap decision entirely: the seven replacement lines are given verbatim, each already at or under 79 columns, with no width to choose. Verified mechanically against the file: block occupies lines 25-31, every line <= 79 characters, the phrase "any console spies a test has installed" on one line, old phrase gone, em dash on the "compiled wasm —" line survives as U+2014, block remains 9 lines (23-31) so the beforeEach stays at 32 and no line number below the block moves. v1's line-number citations are dropped in favour of invariants, as the reviewer asked.

Objection 2 (AC-2 could not fail): accepted, AC-2 withdrawn. Every command in its how_to_verify tested the beforeAll and test bodies — code the change does not touch — so it passed before the diff and could not be made false by it. The greps are kept but demoted: they are the factual underpinning inside AC-1's how_to_verify and repeated as a read-check in qa_script step 3. The only remaining criterion about prose is AC-1, which asserts on the comment text itself.

Finding 1 (the defect this issue can fix). packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:25 reads "installed along with the console spies", where "installed" has as its subject the fetch spy the beforeAll installed. A reader can attach the console clause to "installed" and conclude the beforeAll installs console spies. It does not: beforeAll (lines 17-21) is "beforeAll(async () => { patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL); return init({ baseURL }); });" and `sed -n '17,21p' ... | grep -c console` returns 0; patchFetchForSqlJS touches only global.fetch. The file's own describe-level comment at lines 46-51 already states the correct fact, contradicting the reading line 25 permits. Verified here: five spyOn(console, ...) sites, grep -n returning 81, 116, 160, 311, 379, and 10 it(...) tests. Only occurrence of the phrasing in the repo.

One correction to the review's evidence, carried forward so it does not propagate: there are five console spies, not four. The fifth is the one wrapped across three lines (115-117) that a single-line search for "vi.spyOn(console" misses, and it is the second of the five sites, not the fifth. Any check written against "the fifth at 116-118" is written against a range that does not exist as such.

Finding 2 (release note keep-or-drop). upcoming-release-notes/clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md is on main and validates (Maintenance in categoryOrder at packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs:17-22; Shivam-Fl not in NON_PERSON_AUTHORS at line 30; one-line body). The review is right the cited gate is inert (.github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml exists, no workflow references it). Kept, on other grounds — see approach.

Finding 3 (PR #67 lacks the [AI] prefix). Reproduces as a fact (gh pr view 67 --json title returns "fix: Follow-ups from #58: 2 from the review", merged 2026-10-04), but the title is not hand-authored: .sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs:138 builds it as `fix: ${issueData.title}` with no [AI] anywhere in that file, which is why PRs #53, #59, #60, #64 and #65 share the shape. .sdlc/bin/** is forbidden_paths (.sdlc/config.yml:218). Out of scope, with the location named.
work_order.root_cause: Finding 1 is a dangling-preposition attachment in prose: "along with the console spies" can bind to "installed" rather than to "takes down", producing a claim about the beforeAll that the code contradicts. Nothing executes wrongly — the sentence is wrong, not the test. Finding 2 is not a defect but an open judgement the review declined to close. Finding 3 is a one-line omission in the pipeline's own PR-opening code, outside this repository's changeable surface. The two objections to the v1 plan were defects in the plan, not the code: v1 specified a wrap width that could break its own acceptance check, and v1's second criterion tested only code the change does not touch.
work_order.approach:
One comment-only edit, one file, seven lines replaced by seven lines. Nothing else changes; no file is added or deleted and no behaviour moves.

The fix is the review's first option (move the console clause off "installed" so the attachment is explicit), not the second (drop the clause), because lines 46-51 carry the count but not the beforeAll contrast, and the beforeAll contrast is the whole reason the comment exists — it explains why the beforeEach re-arms a patch the beforeAll already installed.

One deliberate divergence from the review's suggested wording: it proposed "...along with the console spies each test installs". That introduces a fresh factual error — only 5 of the 10 tests install a console spy, so "each test installs" is false of the other five. This order uses "any console spies a test has installed", true now and still true if a sixth test grows a spy. AC-1 grep 3 and qa_script step 4 fail the PR if the reviewer's wording appears.

The replacement text is given verbatim, not described. v1 said "rewrap at most 79 columns" and that instruction is what its own acceptance check failed against; this order leaves nothing to rewrap and nothing to choose.

On finding 2: KEEP the note. The review is right the original justification does not hold, but the note does not need it, and dropping it is the more disruptive. Three reasons, in the order they decided it: (a) the convention that asks for the note is documented and gate-independent — packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md lists "Add a release note" as a PR step and exempts the Maintenance category from the non-technical rule, the one thing this note's body would otherwise breach; (b) the note is already merged, so deleting it is a new PR whose entire content is removing an entry from a changelog about to be published — more visible to readers than the note ever was, and the review's "PR #55 did" comparison does not carry over because #55 never had a note to remove; (c) recursion — a PR whose only content is deleting a release note is itself a change the convention wants a note for.

Recorded as a decision rather than deferred, because the implementer must not be left to make it. Review may disagree cheaply: the note's category, author and body all validate today. What is NOT upheld is the original reasoning — the gate argument is wrong and must not be repeated in the commit message.

On finding 3: no file changes; see out_of_scope.

work_order.debate_summary:
No decisions were recorded for this issue — plan/brief.md is empty on that count — so there was nothing binding to work from. The planning judgement was concentrated in finding 2, where the review explicitly declined to close a call and handed it forward: whether the release note stays now that the gate justifying it turns out to be inert. I closed it (keep) rather than deferring, because the implementer must not be left to make a product-voice judgement, and recorded the reasoning so review can reverse it cheaply. I diverged from the review's suggested replacement wording on finding 1, because that wording introduces a factual error the review itself did not check for.

This version is a response to the rejection, not a defence of v1. Both objections are accepted without qualification. Objection 1: v1's wrap instruction could produce a correct-looking diff that fails v1's own AC-1, and the reviewer's width analysis shows the permitted band overlaps the width this block already uses — the fix is to remove the wrap decision, not to narrow it, so the seven replacement lines are given verbatim and mechanically checked. Objection 2: v1's AC-2 tested only code the diff does not touch, so it passed before the change and could not fail after it; it is withdrawn, and the invariant it carried is kept as AC-1's factual underpinning plus a qa_script read-check. The corpus of line-number citations across v1's criteria is dropped in favour of invariants, since the verbatim block keeps the same 9 lines and therefore the same numbers anyway.
residual_risks: A comment-only change carries a near-zero chance of breaking behaviour, and correspondingly a near-zero chance that the suite catches a mistake in it. AC-1 and AC-2 are the only real checks; AC-1 now greps the text this change writes, so it can fail, but if QA skips it because nothing failed, the change is unverified in the only sense that matters for it.

The release-note decision is the one part of this order a reasonable person could reverse after the fact. It is reversible at no cost — a single validated file that can be deleted whole in a later PR — but if reversed, the changelog changes and that later PR should say so.

review.title: The PR title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix, which the repo's own rules require on every pull request; the work order's out_of_scope reasoning conflates 'the generator cannot be fixed in this repo' with 'this PR's title cannot be fixed', and the remedy costs one command and touches no file.
review.detail:
The PR title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix, which the repo's own rules require on every pull request; the work order's out_of_scope reasoning conflates 'the generator cannot be fixed in this repo' with 'this PR's title cannot be fixed', and the remedy costs one command and touches no file.

`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md:11`

Evidence: `gh pr view 73 --json title -q .title` returns `fix: Follow-ups from #66: 3 from the review` — no `[AI]`. .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md states 'ALL pull request titles MUST be prefixed with `[AI]` — you have to apply it yourself', and the branch's own commit message does carry it (`[AI] Attribute the console spies to the tests that install them`), so the omission is in the PR title alone. The work order's out_of_scope entry argues this is 'not a change this repository can make' because .sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs:138 builds the title as `fix: ${issueData.title}`; I confirmed both halves of that (line 138 has no `[AI]`; .sdlc/config.yml:218 lists `.sdlc/bin/**` under forbidden_paths). But forbidden_paths governs edits to *files in the repository*; renaming an already-open PR is a metadata operation (`gh pr edit 73 --title "[AI] ..."`) that changes no file and is therefore not gated at all. The scope claim is true about fixing the generator and false about fixing this PR.

Fix: Rename the PR to `fix: [AI] Follow-ups from #66: 3 from the review` (or `[AI] fix: ...` to match the commit's placement). Fixing open-pr.mjs:138 stays out of scope and stays with the pipeline owner, exactly as the work order says — but the pipeline owner is not the only one who can put the prefix on this PR.
